StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single, and the sim leaves Power.on_stack alone, so both sides add on re-application -- PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 has no StackType branch and Single only means 'Amount is hidden' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13). Correct, unlike the 15 units that override on_stack to a no-op citing the same StackType (py tools/audit/power_census.py stack). Inert either way: nothing reads Diamond Diadem's Amount on either side -- it is a flat halving that lasts one enemy turn -- and the sole ported applier (relics/diamond_diadem.py:37) applies 1 once per qualifying turn end, removing it before the next application.

ModifyDamageMultiplicative.rationale: 0.5 for powered attacks against the owner, 1 otherwise. Both C# guards are present, one structurally: target != base.Owner (DiamondDiademPower.cs:23-26 vs powers.py:2729-2730) and !props.IsPoweredAttack() (:27-30), which the sim gets from DamageCmd.deal gating the multiplier families on is_powered_attack (cmds.py:56-58) -- the sim's own comment at powers.py:2727-2728 says so. 0.5 is dyadic, so this power does not widen hook_dispatch's G9 (executed: py tools/audit/power_census.py multipliers, which lists it among the safe factors).

AfterSideTurnEnd.rationale: CORRECT SLOT. Like NoBlockPower, DiamondDiademPower.cs:34-40 has no participants filter -- it Removes whenever side == CombatSide.Enemy -- so the sim's side-scoped on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345, the Hook.AfterTurnEnd(Enemy) slot at CombatManager.cs:1256) is exactly right and there is no per-creature question to lose. Remove, not Decrement, on both sides. The sim's _expire (powers.py:86-92) pops the power and unregisters it; C#'s PowerCmd.Remove (PowerCmd.cs:287-295) additionally fires power.AfterRemoved, which this power does not implement. Observationally identical, same treatment as the _expire entries in audits/power/duplication.json and audits/power/flame_barrier.json per binding rule 3.

guards.rationale: DiamondDiadem.cs grants the power at turn end only when the player played few enough cards; the ported relic reproduces that (relics/diamond_diadem.py:33-37, applier=player). That condition belongs to audits/relic/diamond_diadem and is not re-judged here. The POWER's own behaviour is audited in full above.

Neither side latches a command the way power/gigantification does, so the 0.5 applies to every hit of a multi-hit attack independently, and integer truncation happens per hit on both sides (C# rounds the decimal at the damage site, the sim at cmds.py:58's int()). Same observable for the ported content.
